body.name: normalized auxiliary-invariant fuzzy hypotheses
body.construction:
Let \(\ell=\log(en)\), let
\[
C_0=\frac{4}{\log(8/e)},\qquad L=\lceil C_0\ell\rceil,
\]
and put \(M=4n+4(n+m)\).  Define
\[
\kappa=\frac{1-2\epsilon}{\epsilon},\qquad
B=\frac{L}{24M},\qquad
a=\frac{\gamma_\epsilon B}{L^2},\qquad
I=[a/\kappa,B],
\]
where
\[
D_\epsilon=\frac{\kappa}{(1+\kappa)(2+\kappa)},\qquad
\gamma_\epsilon=\min\{\kappa/8,D_\epsilon\kappa/20\}.
\]
Let \(\sigma\) be the finite signed measure furnished by degree-\(L\) approximation duality for \(f(p)=p/(p+a)\) on \(I\), normalized by \(|\sigma|(I)=1\), \(\int p^j\,d\sigma(p)=0\) for \(0\le j\le L\), and \(\int f\,d\sigma\ge D_\epsilon/4\).  Write \(h=d\sigma/d|\sigma|\in\{-1,1\}\) on its finite support and define
\[
\nu(dp)=\frac{a}{p+a}|\sigma|(dp)\quad(p\in I),\qquad
\nu(\{0\})=1-\int_I\frac{a}{p+a}|\sigma|(dp).
\]
Choose
\[
k=\min\{d-1,\lfloor(n+m)L\rfloor\}.
\]
Draw \(p_1,\ldots,p_k\) independently from \(\nu\), put
\[
p_*=1-kE_\nu[p],\qquad S=p_*+\sum_{i=1}^k p_i,
\]
and normalize the \(k\) rare masses and the reservoir mass by \(S\); all unused alphabet cells receive mass zero.  At a positive rare mass set
\[
e(p)=\epsilon(1+a/p),\qquad \mu_0=0,\qquad
\mu_{1,+}=(1+h(p))/2,\qquad \mu_{1,-}=(1-h(p))/2.
\]
At a zero rare mass use identical arbitrary legal conditional values, and at the reservoir use propensity \(1/2\) and both outcome means zero.  The laws of the resulting normalized random observed-data laws are \(\Pi_1\) and \(\Pi_0\), respectively.  These priors are used in the dimension-dominant regime isolated in the converse proof; the complementary regime is covered directly by the known-marginal parametric lower bound.
